Made for Niz to film alone

One performer. One camera operator. Both Niz.

Niz performs, films, resets and judges every episode. No guest, camera operator, live coach, off-camera helper, required online opponent or public interaction is part of the premise. Supplies are bought before filming.

Every new idea is paired with the actual thumbnail from a directly linked source video and a composition note for Niz. Source creators are visual references only; every proposed shoot stays solo. The original 100-image gallery remains below.

Solo format 01 / 5 videos

The solo test bench

One claim, a visible test and a result viewers can judge for themselves.

Niz only · self-filmedProduction plan ↗

Why this format + how to film it

Title shape: I Tested ___ / Can ___ Really ___?

Retention structure: Prediction → repeatable test → unexpected failure → one changed variable → final verdict.

Solo setup: Niz starts a locked desk-wide shot, performs each test in frame and records his own close-ups afterward. Timers and score sheets replace a judge.

Editing rule: Show the control and result in the same framing. Retain failed attempts; label pickup shots and avoid implying a controlled scientific result.

Two channels above 2× support the broad test/bust format. Neither source establishes a solo workflow or predicts results for these desk experiments.

Idea 101 · Niz only

I Tested 5 Dollar-Store Gaming Hacks

Niz tests five cheap desk fixes and keeps only the ones that solve a visible gaming problem.

$15–$30 incremental cash3–4 hours

Opening, solo shoot and payoff
  1. 0 (First Frame)–5sA cable snags mid-move beside five numbered mystery fixes.
  2. 5s–15sShow the snag test and announce that every fix gets the same ten passes.
  3. 15s–30sTry the first fix immediately and put its success count on screen.

Film it alone: Use one fixed side angle to show the cable and mouse; reset each test yourself and add hand close-ups later.

Final payoff: Rank all five fixes by successful passes and actual spend.

Roblox worlds on one desk

Turn a recognizable Roblox world into a small physical object in one room.

Niz only · self-filmedProduction plan ↗

Why this format + how to film it

Title shape: I Built ___ Using Only ___

Retention structure: Recognizable target → empty work surface → material problem → visible improvement → final reveal.

Solo setup: Niz works at one table with a fixed wide view. He stops recording to move the camera for detail shots; time-lapse and self-recorded narration cover construction.

Editing rule: Every build montage must change the object visibly. Save the finished match-cut for the payoff, then show what still falls short.

Two adjacent IRL channels exceed 2× for the broad build/reveal format. Miniature scale and the Niz-specific Roblox ingredients are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated source production methods.

Solo format 03 / 5 videos

My day has game rules

A visible game rule changes Niz’s own afternoon without needing another person.

Niz only · self-filmedProduction plan ↗

Why this format + how to film it

Title shape: I Let ___ Control My ___ / I Turned ___ Into ___

Retention structure: Simple rule → first inconvenience → a tradeoff → mounting progress → final score.

Solo setup: Use prewritten rules, a timer, dice or a self-operated wheel. Niz films room-wide actions and records short check-ins; no audience votes or off-camera instructions are required.

Editing rule: Keep the rule and progress visible. Compress travel and repeated resets; preserve the choice that changes the next scene.

Two channels above 2× support an external rule shaping a day. The solo scripts use self-operated mechanics instead of another participant; that production substitution has not been audience-tested.

Retention structure: Visible contrast → guess → identical tests → price reveal → value decision.

Solo setup: Niz labels A and B and performs both trials sequentially from a locked position. It is an open comparison, not a blind test; nobody else is needed to hide the prices.

Editing rule: Keep test duration and task consistent. Distinguish personal preference from measured time or performance; do not imply that one short test proves a product universally better.

Two adjacent channels above 2× support broad price-contrast packaging. These smaller home comparisons use different products and stakes; exact price points and audience response remain unvalidated.

Solo format 05 / 5 videos

One day, one new skill

Start with an honest failed baseline and finish with one visible, modest skill target.

Niz only · self-filmedProduction plan ↗

Why this format + how to film it

Title shape: Can I Learn ___ in 24 Hours?

Retention structure: Baseline failure → small milestone → plateau → one technique change → final uninterrupted attempt.

Solo setup: Niz teaches himself from written or prerecorded resources and films with a locked wide shot. A 24-hour calendar window allows sleep and ordinary breaks; only 2–4 hours of practice are planned.

Editing rule: Keep a failed final attempt if that is the result. Do not title the episode as mastery; separate best practice clips from the final scored attempt.

These two learning-format references are 1.25× and 1.24×, below the 2× outlier threshold. The format is a low-cost editorial experiment, not a proven outlier; Niz’s noob-to-pro gaming vocabulary is the proposed audience bridge.

03 / Keep a live question

Creative

Practical hook types and ways to carry the episode.

These are proposed IRL adaptations of visible niche formats and the intelligence system. Their effectiveness needs an episode test; the measured moment evidence is in Post-Production.

Recognition → unexpected real version

Audience question: A familiar game mechanic happens in a physical setting.

Show the game and its physical counterpart immediately; establish one changed rule; deliver a small result before widening the challenge.

Ideas 11–18, 89–90 · Niche reference: ROBLOX MUKBANG DATE vs IN REAL LIFE ASMR!

Forced choice

Audience question: Viewers choose before the creator does.

Put both options on screen; allow a short guess window; reveal the consequence and use it to create the next decision.

Ideas 12, 16–17, 46, 73, 76 · Niche reference: Roblox WOULD YOU RATHER: BABY TOWER!

First meeting / missing person

Audience question: A known voice gains a real face and a new relationship.

Use one familiar cue, show the meeting, then turn it into a shared task rather than an extended greeting.

Ideas 2, 5–7, 49 · Niche reference: I Met Nico in Real Life

Visible consequence

Audience question: The game action changes something real.

Show the consequence prop in frame before the attempt; trigger it immediately after a loss; keep a score so each round changes the situation.

Ideas 21–29, 44, 55 · Niche reference: If I DIE I Eat SOUR CANDY in MM2

Contrast you can test

Audience question: Two options invite a verdict the viewer can check.

Use the same task, framing and judging criteria on both sides; reveal actual costs after an initial guess.

Ideas 30, 36, 64, 67, 69, 97 · Niche reference: $1 vs $10,000 HOTEL (ft. Mia)

Transformation with a deadline

Audience question: A visible starting problem must become a finished result.

Show the before state and recipient need; identify a deadline; reveal meaningful progress instead of a shopping montage.

Ideas 14, 40–41, 52, 60 · Niche reference: Surprising Zoey With Her Dream Gaming Setup

Social disagreement

Audience question: Two people interpret the same evidence differently.

Start with conflicting answers; let each give one concise reason; resolve with an observable answer or let the unresolved judgment become the point.

Ideas 4, 8–10, 42, 50–51, 78 · Niche reference: NEVER HAVE I EVER (ft. Mia)

Uncertainty in a bounded location

Audience question: A clear objective is interrupted by a specific unknown.

Show the environment before the scare, establish the task and rules, then preserve enough quiet for a real change to register.

Ideas 39, 81–86, 89 · Niche reference: Keep Your Door LOCKED in ROBLOX at 3AM...

Three ways to structure a full episode

Rounds with consequences

For quizzes, food and crew games: promise → simple first round → harder choice → changed score → final contest. Each result changes the next attempt. Keep one score graphic and remove repeated rules.

A task in the real world

For builds, shifts and travel: visible goal → first attempt → real obstacle → revised approach → finished result. Cut transport that changes nothing; keep a person correcting Niz or a decision that changes the route.

Access through a relationship

For family and meetups: recognition → shared task → disagreement or surprise → a revealing story → something they accomplish together. A guest introduction earns its length through action.

First-frame contract: The pictured people, object or dilemma should be visible immediately. By 15 seconds the rule and stakes should be clear; by 30 seconds a real attempt should be underway. These are writing targets, not measured universal retention thresholds.

Re-hook after each payoff

Show what changed, then open the next specific question. Use a harder round, a shrinking budget, a newly revealed clue or a guest taking control. Avoid a new promise that the episode never answers, long resets after a win, and repeated shouting that adds no information.

Five formats that work with Niz alone

For these proposed series, an object, rule, timer or personal target supplies the tension. Each has five fully outlined episodes in Ideation.

FormatEpisode structureEditing decision
The solo test benchState the claim; establish a control; run three to five tests; retry the surprising result; finish with a useful verdict.Show the control and result in the same framing. Retain failed attempts; label pickup shots and avoid implying a controlled scientific result.
Roblox worlds on one deskReveal the reference and constraints; block out the shape; expose one honest setback; solve it; match the finished object to the reference.Every build montage must change the object visibly. Save the finished match-cut for the payoff, then show what still falls short.
My day has game rulesDemonstrate the rule immediately; apply it to three different situations; track every exception; finish with a score and a real personal verdict.Keep the rule and progress visible. Compress travel and repeated resets; preserve the choice that changes the next scene.
Cheap versus premium, same testUnbox both together; set three relevant criteria; test in the same framing; reveal actual receipts; decide what he would keep.Keep test duration and task consistent. Distinguish personal preference from measured time or performance; do not imply that one short test proves a product universally better.
One day, one new skillDefine success before practice; show the baseline; film three checkpoints; show the hardest setback; finish on a timed or counted attempt.Keep a failed final attempt if that is the result. Do not title the episode as mastery; separate best practice clips from the final scored attempt.

Solo coverage: Record the real attempt from a fixed wide angle, then film your own close-ups and a short explanation of what changed. Keep the result visible without needing a reaction from someone else.

05 / Edit from the measured moments

Post-Production

MoreNizarisaqt retention curves and timestamped decisions.

The source catalogue contains 475 retention curves. This explorer selects 28 relevant videos with annotated moments: guessing games, horror, night shifts, progression and survival. Dashboard pull: September 5, 2026; data through September 3. Open the channel analysis →

Watch this timestamp ↗Full source analysis →

The curve plots the source watch ratio, which can exceed 100% when sections are replayed. Times and 5s/15s/30s values interpolate the available percentage-duration samples; they are not second-by-second event measurements. Green markers are source-tagged peaks; coral markers are source-tagged drops. A tagged drop may still outperform the usual drop at that position.

What to carry into an IRL edit

Show the solution, then advance

Singer Tower at 6:20 records a sustained rise through five samples (+0.9% of viewers present in the source annotation). Keep the solved state legible. At 6:51, the post-verdict aside has a 2.3× normal stop rate. Test a shorter bridge into the next question.

Source and caveats →

Keep a strong reaction connected to an outcome

The 6:45 Adele verdict in the same video shows a one-sample +5.6% rise among viewers present. At 3:53, a scream transition has a 2.6× normal stop rate. The practical test is a clear verdict followed by the next choice, with reaction length earned by the result.

Review the 6:45 moment →

Distinguish a reveal from the reset after it

Mining Factory marks the unlock at 6:49 as a peak and the following 6:56 segment as a drop. Preserve the reward and inspect the transition into another purchase or grind. For a real build, reveal the working upgrade before moving on.

Inspect both moments →

Review interruptions and repeated effort

Grow a Chicken Fighter flags 7:41 around a subscribe/like aside. Drain Water flags a shop/menu moment at 10:29 and a grind admission at 15:55. Trial cuts should retain the relevant decision while shortening repeated explanation.

Review the source →

Moment patterns across the channel

The source grouped 119 usable moments from 36 of 40 recent analyzed videos. No category had a consistent effect. The adjusted percentage-point values below compare flagged moments with the typical flagged moment of the same kind and video position; they are not a promised lift in overall retention.

Tagged moment typeAdjusted median effectMoments / videosp-valueEdit implication to test
Viewers scrub back+1.9 pp26 / 16.152Keep the payoff legible; a replay can also signal confusion.
Scripted / NPC dialogue+1.3 pp13 / 9.267Keep dialogue that changes a choice; trim repetitive exposition.
Reveal / pull / unlock+0.8 pp10 / 81.000Preserve the reveal and shorten the reset afterward.
Explaining plan / setup+0.4 pp8 / 81.000Show the rule while action begins.
Tangent / aside0.0 pp19 / 121.000Judge the specific aside; the category alone gives no answer.
Shop / menu−0.2 pp12 / 10.774Keep the purchase decision, compress navigation.
Combat / boss−0.4 pp13 / 10.774Clarify the objective and what each attempt changes.
Grind / rebirth admission−1.9 pp6 / 61.000Replace repeated effort with progress and a fresh target.
Mistake / failure−2.4 pp12 / 11.774Keep consequences; avoid repeating an unchanged failure.

Groups are observational and small. First-30-second/coarse/unusable moments were excluded by the source. These are gaming-channel patterns to test in IRL, not established IRL retention laws.

Editor handoff

  1. Mark the promised payoff and the next unanswered question in every scene.
  2. Review 15 seconds on each side of a flagged moment; distinguish confusing action, a rewind, an ad break and a spent payoff.
  3. Make one specific proposed change, keep the original cut, and record what would support or disprove it.
  4. After release, compare early retention and relative performance at matched video positions; do not attribute a whole-video result to one cut.
06 / Turn one beat into a complete Short

Shorts Strategy

Creators in Niz’s niche: Foltyn and Lana’s Life.

Live public Shorts shelves checked September 24, 2026: 48 visible Shorts per channel. Counts are rounded lifetime views, not engaged views, retention or conversion to long-form. Sample medians: Foltyn 8.15M; Lana’s Life 2.10M. Ratios compare only this visible shelf, are not age-adjusted outlier scores, and do not prove why a Short worked.

Game mechanic performed in real life

Hook: Show the recognizable game action in a real room before explaining it.

Niz version: One Steal a Brainrot raid in the brother’s room; the guard turns around at the worst time.

Need / cost: $20–100 incremental; 1–2 people, 30–60 minutes, one recognizable prop.

Proposed timing: 0–2s: recognizable action. 2–12s: the real-world obstacle. 12–25s: outcome and a visual callback.

Creator contest with a single measurable result

Hook: Put both contestants and the scoring device in the first frame.

Niz version: Niz versus brother: one penalty kick each, one visible score.

Need / cost: $0–60 if already together; 2–3 people, 20–40 minutes. Venue access is extra.

Proposed timing: 0–2s: question and contestants. 2–15s: attempts. 15–25s: result and reaction.

Recognizable game food, real taste test

Niz version: One Roblox food beside its real version, then brother guesses which tastes better.

07 / Sources, scope and the original research

Data Analysis

Keep the numbers auditable.

32 ideas meet the two-channel target on both axes within this pool. Others retain explicit gaps, weaker comparisons or unscored matches. Separate Niz channels share a creator, and Cash/Nico examples share a cast ecosystem, so channel counts do not mean independent audiences. Six adjacent IRL challenge channels broaden the search; their evidence cards explicitly flag the audience transfer.

How the intelligence and attached guides were applied

The public intelligence system supplies familiar-plus-mystery, credible stakes and the first-frame promise. The two attached thumbnail documents supply expectation match, one dominant subject, restrained visual groups, contrast, mobile readability and concrete frameworks. The user’s instruction to closely preserve each reference composition controls this revision; guide suggestions inform the adaptation rather than imposing a new generic style.

  • Intelligence-system source and general claims: rules are distinguished from observations and theories.
  • 10 Rules of Thumbnails: use the filmed premise, complementary title/visual information and an appropriate facial reaction.
  • 16 Engaging Thumbnail Frameworks: comparison, transformation, portrait, social UI, compelling scene, product and progression appear in the Packaging library.
Original channel, launch, sequencing and method research

Preserved September 9/10 snapshot. Historical subscriber counts, projections, score denominators and old language below are retained for provenance; use the revised evidence above for decisions.

The template

What Cash and Nico did at the start

Cash Marco was created on 2023-10-21 as Cash's real-life channel, a year after the Cash Minecraft channel. Nico Polo followed in October 2024, launched around Nico's face reveal on the main channel. The first five uploads on both contain the same three videos: a day in the life (upload one on both), meeting the other half of the duo in real life (upload two on Cash Marco, upload three on Nico Polo), and a look at where they live (Cash's apartment tour at three; Nico's setup and mansion at four and five). The day-in-the-life video read 1.36x on Cash Marco and 0.52x on Nico Polo; the meeting was the biggest video of each launch.

What happened next separates them. Cash Marco went into a hundred and eleven uploads of solo reaction content (Skibidi Toilet watch-alongs, Dhar Mann-style story reactions, tier lists, 100% playthroughs) at a median of 1.1M views, then stopped, came back with "I'M BACK..." and ran twenty-three videos with Nico, Shady, Mia and Zoey in the room at a median of 4.1M. The channel has not uploaded since 2025-06-14. Nico Polo never left the cast: forty-nine uploads whose titles name Cash, Zoey, Foltyn, Lana, his crush or his family in most of them, a six-month pause from August 2025, and a weekly schedule since May 2026 at 2M a video.

The template in one line. Open with the face, the partner and the room; keep the cast in every video; spend the "I Met" shape on the biggest name who will say yes, about once a month; run the cheap constraint and party formats in between; launch at ten to fifteen minutes and lengthen only when the numbers say so.

Three things the library says that the ideas below are built on. The cast shapes are the biggest and the least portable: the party games read 2.14x across 15 uploads, but 7.86x with Cash's cast and 1.09x with Nico's two, so the number belongs to the people as much as the shape. The constraint shapes are the most portable: living in a car reads 2.70x on three uploads across both channels, and the eating constraints are above median on both. And repeats decay: the second home-alone horror video read 0.21x, the second first-class flight 0.65x, the second reacting-to-TikToks 1.21x against a 2.36x first run.

The raw material

What Nizar already has

He shows his face on every thumbnail already, so there is no reveal to stage. His little brother is on camera and reads above median when Nizar is upgrading him or being judged by him (1.90x, 1.68x, 1.37x) and below it when Nizar trolls him in-game (0.58x, 0.46x). Rex, his duo partner, runs his own 97K channel. His audience has voted for real-life ingredients inside the Roblox videos: the sour-candy penalty is his biggest outlier of 2026 at 5.50x, Guess The Country a 3.48x breakout on MoreNizarisaqt, exposing his own secrets read 2.94x, sneaking into other YouTubers' videos 2.67x, and reacting to their TikToks about him 2.27x. He is Moroccan and the identity angle has three readings above median.

The repo's measured constraints on MoreNizarisaqt carry over. Thirty-one percent of the audience leaves in the first five percent of a video, which is the channel's largest single loss, so the IRL videos open on what the thumbnail showed. The share still watching at halfway falls with runtime (r = -0.75 over 40 uploads), which is the second reason to launch at ten to fifteen minutes. Click-through sits at 8.9% and 62% of classified viewers return, which is the audience the IRL channel is asking to follow it. The Nizarisaqt IRL channel was created on 2024-02-17, has 76K subscribers, features the main channel's "I Bought My DREAM HOUSE..." upload (1.30x, 315K) as its trailer, and has never uploaded.

The knowledge base's warning that a video which misrepresents the channel delivers subscribers who want something you do not make is the reason the IRL content belongs on the separate channel that already exists, and the reason the bridge videos in the second family are the only ones that should touch the main channel.

Packaging

What the reference thumbnails have in common

The launch and crew thumbnails on Cash Marco and Nico Polo share a template that is nearly the opposite of the Roblox one: no avatar, no yellow text block, no arrows to game objects. The original thumbnail briefs used that template. The generated concepts below also apply the supplied thumbnail guides, varying the framework and expression to suit each idea.

Real faces, plain teesTwo or three people in single bright colours, looking at the lens. "I Met" thumbnails are two faces and a name.
One propThe car, the blindfold, the sign, the tray. Never two.
Three words or fewer"HOUR 19", "SHADY", "$15,000". The Roblox thumbnails carry a sentence; these carry a label.
An arrow only for a personThe red arrow names the guest. It never points at an object.
Keep his reaction faceThe one thing that carries over: the open-mouth face on every Nizarisaqt thumbnail is the same face on Cash's and Nico's.
Subject against backgroundThe knowledge base's legibility warning: bright tee, plain wall, nothing the same colour as the person.

Sequencing

The first ten uploads, in order

The order both reference channels used, corrected by what their own catalogues later said. Weekly, the way Nico Polo runs now; the "I Met" tentpole lands at the end of the first month so that the first three weeks have already made the face and the room familiar.

  1. #1 A Day in the Life of Nizar (15 Videos a Week)Mirrors upload 1 on both reference channels. Eight to ten minutes.
  2. #2 I Met Rex in Real LifeMirrors upload 2 on both: the duo partner walks in. The tentpole shape, spent on the person the audience already knows.
  3. #3 House Tour: Where 15 Videos a Week Get MadeMirrors Cash's upload 3. The IRL channel already features the Dream House video, so the tour is the follow-up it promised.
  4. #21 Eating Only SOUR Candy for 24 HoursThe main channel's biggest outlier of the year, taken out of the game. The face on the thumbnail is the one that already works.
  5. #4 My Little Brother Reads My Hate CommentsCash's upload 4, with the correction his own catalogue supplies: a second person tripled it.
  6. #13 Roblox Mukbang vs Real-Life MukbangThe bridge video: the one hybrid shape measured on the Roblox channels themselves (3.27x on Kat). Also a candidate for the main channel that week.
  7. #8 Who Knows Nizar Better? Brother vs RexCheap, two contestants, one evening. The first cast video.
  8. #31 Living in My Car for 24 HoursThe first constraint video: three readings on two channels, all above median.
  9. #51 Reacting to Your TikToks About Me (With My Brother)His own 2.27x, run once on the new channel where it is new again; the repeat measured 0.62x.
  10. #5 I Met Cash & Nico in Real LifeThe month-one tentpole. The guest's size is the variable, and the audience has already voted on YouTuber crossovers at 2.67x.

What to measure after the tenth upload: the IRL channel's own median, which replaces the 265K base in every projection; whether the main channel's returning-viewer share moved; and which of the ten sat above the new median, because that is the first reading of which family this audience follows.

Claims

The knowledge-base claims the cards lean on

Standing as the intelligence pages record it. A law is signed; a warning is a failure mode someone has seen; a theory is unmeasured; measured means the repo's own probes; observed means a count made on this page.

law Three convergent examplesThe more independent examples you find sharing the same angle of expectation, the more likely it is a repeatable format rather than one creator's win. Around three convergent examples is usually enough to act on.
law One winner isn't a formatA single winner does not establish a format: the win may belong to the subject, the guest, a timing event or one package. Repetition is what proves it.
law Packaging outweighs retentionPackaging outweighs retention as a driver of views by a very large margin; a high-retention video with weak packaging can be dwarfed by a low-retention video with strong packaging.
warning Announcement videos are weakestAnnouncement, promo and channel-update videos are the weakest format on a channel by views and watch time, unless the creator's life is itself the product.
warning Life as the productThe announcement penalty depends on whether the creator's life is itself the product: on Her2Wheels a channel update posted the channel's highest CTR.
warning Compilations underperformAftermath and compilation content, the cleanup after the interesting part or a recut of existing footage, underperforms with the existing audience.
warning Match the scaleAn outlier score alone is not sufficient to green-light an idea: TAM must match the channel's current scale.
warning Format without variablesBranding repeats while episodes contain no meaningfully different inputs or results: the audience contract survives but the uncertainty that justified watching does not.
warning Same job or no adjacencyAn adjacency is only valid when the two audiences perform the same verb-object job; sharing a noun or a demographic is a false adjacency.
warning Vector must change eventsA broadly legible object or status marker only works when it materially changes the events or payoff; bolted on, it is empty packaging.
warning Stakes must be credibleFake consequences are discounted by viewers, while the threat of embarrassment or visible failure is sufficient.
warning Stay unscriptedFabricated obstacles trigger a credibility failure and unscripted content that plants one can be caught on a continuity error.
observed Repeats decayed hereSecond runs of the same premise read 0.21x to 0.65x on Cash Marco and Nico Polo where the first run read 1.4x to 3.0x. Observed on this page, not a knowledge-base claim.
measured Repeats don't wear outThe repo tested whether repeating a shape wears it out, on 15 channels. It did not. The action lists on both Nizarisaqt pages rest on it.
theory The swap testTake the source channel's outliers and ask whether the concept keeps its novelty and humour with your subject substituted in; formats rooted in specifically human relationships fail it for non-players.
theory Cheap formats compoundProduction complexity does not correlate with views, and simple formats outperform partly because they are cheap enough to repeat.
theory Three to five escalating roundsSegment-based videos hold best at three to five rounds with escalating lengths; one round is too thin and many rounds fail without a culminating payoff.
theory Memorable through contrastA creator becomes memorable through contrast with the people around them; casting friends with the same personality erases the creator's distinctiveness.
theory Money is never the motiveMoney is never a motivation by itself; the audience resonates once it is tied to a human need. Last-to-leave money shapes read 0.85x to 0.86x on MrBeast Gaming and Stokes Twins.
theory A serialised worldA channel should be run as a serialised world with recurring characters and a season-level arc; the arc is what makes viewers return rather than merely click.
theory Countdowns holdOn-screen countdown timers and explicit time limits hold retention through otherwise weak visual stretches and encode a promise of something at zero.
law Familiar plus mysteriousTitles that expose a knowledge gap in something the viewer already has a relationship with convert well because no new interest has to be built.
warning Curiosity without importanceA clearly stated unknown whose answer is trivial will click but not satisfy.
warning Work needs stakesContent organised around succeeding at a work task only holds when the occupation is heroic; otherwise the work must be backdrop for personal stakes.
observed Cast carries the shapeThe same party-game shapes read 2.1x to 7.9x on Cash Marco with its cast and 1.0x on Nico Polo with two people; the hate-comments video tripled when a second person read them. Observed on this page.
measured Longer holds less hereOn MoreNizarisaqt the share still watching at halfway falls with runtime (r = -0.75, n = 40); the repo's action is to cut uploads over about twenty minutes.

Limits

What this page cannot say

  • Lifts on Cash Marco and Nico Polo are lifetime views divided by a lifetime median. The knowledge base's law says the fair comparison is each video's first 28 days, which no public source gives; older uploads are flattered and the newest are undercounted.
  • Exact publish dates for the launch-era uploads could not be read: YouTube rate-limited the watch pages on the day of the crawl. Eras are read from the title sequence and the fifteen dated entries in each channel feed.
  • The one-in-three conversion figure rests on two channels and today's subscriber counts. The Roblox channels were smaller when the IRL channels launched, so the launch-time conversion was higher than 0.33 and is unknown.
  • Projections assume the IRL channel's typical upload lands where the main channel's does. The IRL channel has 76K subscribers; its first uploads will land below the base until the audience moves, and the range is the main channel's spread, not the IRL channel's.
  • No retention, click-through or viewer split exists for any IRL channel in the set. Everything about what happens inside these videos is inherited from MoreNizarisaqt's measured curves and the knowledge base's theories.
  • Format classification is by title. A video's shape is what its title claims, which is the package, not the content.
  • The niche-list medians are the latest thirty uploads, which is a week for a daily channel and a year for a slow one; the knowledge base's cadence warning applies.
  • The per-channel "views per upload" figures are over uploads aged 28 to 360 days at the crawl. Only MoreNizarisaqt's are first-28-day views; the others are lifetime views, so a channel whose uploads keep accruing (Nico Polo's do) is flattered against one whose uploads front-load. Cash Marco has no upload inside the window, so its row carries lifetime figures over all 145 uploads.

Method

How the figures were made

Catalogues were read from the public YouTube pages of Cash Marco (UCCbsKLn-kAJR6b_dXtfJj2Q), Nico Polo (UCgmU4jG1sSkpqfZ7h9_gDWA), the Nizarisaqt IRL channel (UCyaqVl5F2E8G6MY-oFyrlEA) and the twenty-two handles on the supplied list on 2026-09-09: titles, lifetime view counts, runtimes and relative upload age, plus the dated channel feeds. Nizarisaqt's and MoreNizarisaqt's figures are the repo's own: outlier scores, the Studio pull on MoreNizarisaqt, the action lists and the format library on the two channel pages. Lift is views divided by the channel's median (lifetime median for the two IRL channels, median of the latest thirty for the niche list, the repo's first-28-day outlier score for Nizar's channels). A shape's lift is the median of its uploads' lifts. An idea's projection is the main channel's median (265K) times the median lift of the uploads cited on its card, with the main channel's quartile spread (0.64x to 1.40x) as the range, which is the arithmetic the channel pages' own idea cards use. Channel profiles (avatar, subscribers, every long-form upload back to 360 days with its lifetime views) were crawled from the public channel pages on 2026-09-10; the evidence thumbnails under Why this idea are the uploads' own, stored beside this page. The 100 generated concept thumbnails were added on 2026-09-11 using the supplied thumbnail guides and the public intelligence snapshot. The ideas and the prose were written by Claude on a human brief; the figures were computed, none typed. The knowledge base's warning that an AI suggestion is never demand evidence applies to all hundred.
